title: Oracle q-quote pre-scan ignores string-literal state and unredacts later SQL literals, including tainted values
claim: scanOracleQuotes treats q'/Q' after a non-identifier byte as an Oracle q-quote even inside an ordinary '...' literal (e.g. 'Q' followed by ','). The bogus span closes at a later <open>' pair, the query is split there, and all dialect lexers resynchronize out of phase so real literal bodies lex as identifiers. A tainted value in such a literal is emitted raw both in the evidence part and as the wire source value, because BuildWithSensitive only redacts sources overlapping a sensitive interval (source.go:66).
repro_command: cp .omo/review/evidence/crash-fuzz-redaction/zz_review_oracle_desync_test.go internal/taint/redaction/ && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test ./internal/taint/redaction/ -run TestReview -count=1 -v

title: SQL comment bodies are not redacted, contrary to the shared normative redaction suite
claim: The shared evidence-redaction-suite (dd-trace-js/dd-trace-py) and dd-trace-java's SqlRegexpTokenizer redact line and block comment bodies; dd-iast-go emits them verbatim and its analyzer test pins 'SELECT column -- secret' as raw. Credentials or tainted fragments in comments leave the process unredacted.

title: FuzzAnalyzeSQL's coverage oracle reuses the production q-quote splitter, so it is blind to F1
claim: assertDefaultSQLLiteralsCovered calls scanOracleQuotes and lexes the same segments as production, so any splitter desync is replicated in the oracle; a 20M-exec 8-minute campaign passed while F1 reproduces with a 70-byte query. The oracle also checks only the default dialect.

title: FuzzMappedPattern checks only length and budget, not the redaction property
claim: A regression returning the raw value of the right length would pass; the corpus stayed at 15 entries over 9.2M execs.

title: FuzzSnapshotCanonicalization never exercises marks, drop bounds or distinct owner generations
claim: All generated ranges have Marks==0, OwnerGen==1, Name==Value, a fixed 16-byte value and at most 32 inputs, so mark-split merging, vulnerability-mark suppression, MaxCollectedRanges drop and source-byte budget drop are never fuzzed.

title: FuzzAdd covers only the isolated string Table.Add path
claim: Production inserts use prepareBytes and transactional managed-source methods; the byte-equality branch and prepare/commit split are not fuzzed, and 300 Sprintf+testify calls per exec keep throughput low.
